summary: This standards-track RFC defines S-BFD for Virtual Circuit Connectivity Verification by extending the procedures and CV types defined for BFD over VCCV. It updates RFC 5885 by extending the CV Type values and capability selection.

eli5.summary: Quick link-health checks for virtual circuits, by adding a few new options to the existing method.

how does s-bfd differ from bfd on pseudowires
subtitle: How Seamless BFD can run over a pseudowire's connectivity-check channel, with two new check types.

tldr.problem: Operators check that a pseudowire still works by running BFD over its VCCV control channel, but the existing CV types only cover ordinary BFD, not Seamless BFD (S-BFD).
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines two new CV Type bits, 0x40 for IP/UDP-encapsulated S-BFD and 0x80 for S-BFD without IP/UDP headers, plus rules for encapsulation, discriminators and choosing between them.
tldr.outcome: S-BFD can be advertised alongside BFD for single-segment pseudowires over MPLS or L2TPv3. The RFC updates RFC 5885.

today: RFC 7885 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted. It updates RFC 5885 by extending its CV Type values and capability selection.

sections.title: Background and Scope
sections.content:
RFC 5885 defines how Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) runs over the Virtual Circuit Connectivity Verification (VCCV) channel of a pseudowire (PW). This document extends those procedures and CV Type values so that Seamless BFD (S-BFD, RFC 7880) can be used the same way.

The new S-BFD CV Types do not depend on the PW demultiplexer, so they apply to both MPLS and L2TPv3 pseudowires. The scope is narrow: single-segment PWs (SS-PWs), S-BFD asynchronous mode only. S-BFD Echo mode, and S-BFD for fault detection with status signaling, are out of scope.

The RFC specifies a single S-BFD discriminator per PW. Several discriminators per PW could help, for example one per flow on a Flow-Aware Transport (FAT) PW, but that would need a flow-to-discriminator mapping first.
sections.eli5: This RFC is only about one kind of virtual cable at a time, and only one simple way of checking it. Fancier checks are left for another day.

sections.title: The Two S-BFD CV Types
sections.content:
S-BFD provides continuity checks by monitoring S-BFD Control packets sent and received over the VCCV channel of the PW. Two CV Types are defined, both for fault detection only: 0x40 for S-BFD with IP/UDP headers, and 0x80 for S-BFD without IP/UDP headers (PW-ACH encapsulation on an MPLS PW, or L2-Specific Sublayer encapsulation on an L2TP PW). The 'fault detection and status signaling' column is not applicable for either.

Because the S-BFD and BFD CV Type values are distinct, a node can advertise BFD and S-BFD capabilities at the same time.
sections.eli5: There are two new kinds of 'are you there?' message. One is wrapped in an internet envelope and one is not. A device can know both the old and new kinds at once.

sections.title: Initiator and Reflector Operation
sections.content:
The S-BFD initiator SHOULD start S-BFD sessions once it has learned the discriminator of the remote target. The RFC lists non-exhaustive ways to learn it: advertisement through a PW signaling protocol (L2TP or LDP), manual provisioning on the PE or L2TP Control Connection Endpoint, assignment by a controller, or probing through a mechanism such as S-BFD Alert Discriminators. The initiator MUST follow Section 7.3 of RFC 7880.

The reflector sends each received packet back over the VCCV channel in the reverse direction of the same PW, since all point-to-point PWs are bidirectional. Demultiplexing uses the PW context, following Section 7.1 of RFC 7880, and the BFD fields are handled as RFC 7880 specifies.

For advertising target discriminators, an L2TP reflector MUST use the AVP defined in RFC 7886. For LDP, the advertisement is left for further study, so signaled PWs over MPLS can still use S-BFD by provisioning or learning discriminators another way. For static PWs, discriminators MAY be provisioned.
sections.eli5: One end asks 'are you there?' using the other end's special name tag. The other end answers straight back along the same cable. The name tag can be told over the cable or written down by hand.

sections.title: S-BFD Encapsulation
sections.content:
Unless stated otherwise, S-BFD packets are encapsulated as in Section 3.2 of RFC 5885 and RFC 5880. Two formats exist.

  • IP/UDP: the destination UDP port MUST be 7784 (RFC 7881), the Control packet contents MUST follow Section 7.3.2 of RFC 7880, and the TTL (IPv4) or Hop Limit (IPv6) is set to 255.
  • PW-ACH/L2SS (no IP/UDP headers): encapsulation follows Section 3.2 of RFC 5885, except for the type value. The Channel Type of the PW-ACH (the PW Control Word) or L2SS MUST be 0x0008, meaning 'S-BFD Control, PW-ACH/L2SS-encapsulated', so the S-BFD payload can be identified when demultiplexing the VCCV control channel.
sections.eli5: The message can travel in a normal internet envelope with a fixed mailbox number, or in a plain wrapper marked with a special stamp so the receiver knows what it is.

sections.title: Capability Selection
sections.content:
After applying the rules in RFC 5885, the two ends of the PW work out which S-BFD CV Types they share. If they share more than one, the one with the lowest list number is used: first 0x40 (IP/UDP-encapsulated), then 0x80 (PW-ACH/L2SS-encapsulated). Both are for fault detection only.

Between S-BFD and BFD, the RFC gives a matrix. If one end offers only BFD and the other only S-BFD, the result is none. If one end offers only BFD and the other offers both, BFD is used. If one end offers only S-BFD and the other offers both, S-BFD is used. If both offer both, the result is both. This is why the RFC says it updates RFC 5885: it extends the CV Type values and the capability selection.
sections.eli5: If both sides know several ways to check, they pick the first one on a shared list. If they have nothing in common, they do not check at all.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The S-BFD CV Types introduce no new security risks for VCCV. Implementations are subject to the same considerations as VCCV in Section 10 of RFC 5085 and those in RFC 7880.

The IP/UDP encapsulation uses the TTL and Hop Limit procedures of the Generalized TTL Security Mechanism (RFC 5082) as a security mechanism.
sections.eli5: Sending the message with its hop counter set to its highest value is a trick that helps the receiver ignore messages that came from far away.

sections.title: IANA Allocations
sections.content:
IANA has added entries in three registries. In the MPLS VCCV Connectivity Verification (CV) Types registry, bit 6 (0x40) is S-BFD IP/UDP-encapsulated and bit 7 (0x80) is S-BFD PW-ACH-encapsulated, both for PW fault detection only. In the L2TPv3 VCCV Capability AVP (Attribute Type 96) Values registry, bit 6 (0x40) is S-BFD IP/UDP-encapsulated and bit 7 (0x80) is S-BFD L2SS-encapsulated.

In the MPLS Generalized Associated Channel (G-ACh) Types registry, the Pseudowire Associated Channel Type 0x0008 is assigned to S-BFD Control, PW-ACH/L2SS encapsulation (without IP/UDP headers).
sections.eli5: The official list of numbers got three new lines, so everyone uses the same numbers for the new message types.
